title: Managing your build from abroad
headline: How to keep control of money and quality when you can’t be on site.
seoTitle: Building a house in Nigeria from abroad: staged payments, proof and supervision
seoDescription: How Nigerians in the diaspora can manage construction back home: staged payments, photo and video proof, avoiding lump-sum transfers and using independent supervision.
summary: Most diaspora build problems are not technical — they are about money moving faster than work. These rules keep them in step.
whatHappens: Agree a written contract with drawings, BOQ, specification, programme and a payment schedule linked to stages — not dates.

Pay in stages, after evidence: e.g. a mobilisation payment, then payments on completion of foundation to DPC, superstructure, roofing, services and finishes. Keep a retention (often 5%) until defects are fixed. [CHECK the split for your project]
Buy key materials against invoices, or pay suppliers directly for big items (rods, cement, roofing), so you know what was bought.
Weekly report: photos and short videos from fixed spots, a list of work done, materials delivered and next week’s plan.
Independent supervision: a quantity surveyor, engineer or project manager who works for you — not the builder — inspects before each payment and before concrete is cast.
Keep a shared folder (Google Drive/WhatsApp archive) of all drawings, receipts, photos and approvals.
problems: Sending one large lump sum ‘to start’ — the most common way money disappears.
Relatives acting as contractor and supervisor at once, with no records.
Photos reused from other sites. Ask for videos with a date and your name said aloud, or a live video call.
Materials ‘bought’ twice or diverted to other jobs.
No written contract, so the scope and price keep changing.
Contractor demanding money urgently for ‘price increases’ with no supplier quotes.
questions: Can we agree payments by completed stage, with evidence, and a retention until handover?
Can you send a weekly report with dated photos/videos from the same positions?
Can I pay the supplier directly for major materials?
Who is the independent supervisor, and will they confirm work before each payment?
How are variations priced and approved in writing?
Where are all receipts and delivery notes kept?
photoCheckpoints: A dated video walk-round each week, starting from the gate.
Photos of every delivery with the delivery note or invoice in the frame.
Before-and-after photos for every stage payment request.
A live video call before you release any payment above an agreed amount.
The independent supervisor’s signed inspection note for each stage.
